name: OSQAR
full_name: Optical Search for QED vacuum magnetic birefringence, Axions and photon Regeneration
summary: A historical ALP search using laser-photon regeneration in LHC dipole magnets.
detection_principle: Photons convert to ALPs in the first magnetic region, cross a wall, and regenerate as visible light in the second magnetic region.
technologies: Laser light shining through a wall

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2015 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: New Exclusion Limits for the Search of Scalar and Pseudoscalar Axion-Like Particles from Light Shining Through a Wall

collaboration.name: OSQAR Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No regenerated photons; in the near-zero-mass limit, pseudoscalar / scalar couplings are constrained below 3.5 / 3.2×10⁻⁸ GeV⁻¹ respectively (95% CL).

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
